skill.name: ethical-hacking-methodology
skill.description: Teaches the penetration testing lifecycle, including reconnaissance, scanning, vulnerability analysis, exploitation concepts, reporting, and Kali Linux setup guidance.
skill.summary: Guides authorized security assessments from reconnaissance through reporting.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The skill contains operational penetration testing instructions, including network scanning, Metasploit exploitation, credential attacks, persistence, privilege escalation checks, command injection examples, and destructive disk commands. Some keyword-only malware taxonomy and Markdown fence findings are false positives, but multiple confirmed critical findings remain. The skill should not be published until offensive and destructive procedures are removed or constrained to non-operational lab guidance.

remediation.suggestion: Remove Metasploit exploit steps, Meterpreter payloads, SSH key persistence, cron backdoors, and maintaining access instructions. Replace them with high-level defensive concepts.
Remove Hydra brute force examples and password cracking workflows, or restrict them to non-executable descriptions for isolated lab accounts.

remediation.issue: Sensitive file and command injection examples
remediation.suggestion: Remove payloads that access /etc/passwd or enumerate databases with SQLMap. Use benign toy examples without real system paths or data extraction.
Remove dd, gparted, mount, and raw /dev/sdb examples from the marketplace skill, or replace them with warnings and non-executable setup guidance.
Remove advice to use proxies, VPNs, or packet fragmentation when scans are blocked. Replace it with scope review and authorization escalation steps.

content.value_statement: Security learners need a structured path through penetration testing concepts. This skill organizes reconnaissance, scanning, exploitation concepts, reporting, and lab setup into a clear workflow.
actual_capabilities: Outlines reconnaissance, scanning, exploitation, maintaining access, reporting, and ethics phases.
Lists common security tools such as Nmap, Nikto, Gobuster, Metasploit, Hydra, SQLMap, and John.
Provides a report structure with executive summary, technical findings, risk ratings, remediation, and appendices.
Summarizes common attack categories, malware types, and network attacks at a conceptual level.
Describes Kali Linux installation and persistent live USB setup steps.
limitations: Includes offensive commands that require strict authorization and controlled lab use.
Does not verify target ownership, scope, or legal permission.
Does not include safeguards that prevent destructive disk or persistence commands.
Requires security judgment to separate education from operational testing.

use_cases.title: Build a Training Syllabus
use_cases.description: Turn the lifecycle phases into a classroom sequence for authorized labs and report writing practice.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Assessment Plan
use_cases.description: Map reconnaissance, scanning, validation, reporting, and remediation activities before an approved engagement.

use_cases.title: Study Security Terminology
use_cases.description: Review common tools, attack categories, risk ratings, and professional reporting expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Lifecycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the authorized penetration testing lifecycle in simple terms. Include the purpose of each phase and the expected deliverables.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Lab Study Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a four week study plan for a local lab. Keep every activity inside systems that I own or have written permission to test.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Report Outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a professional penetration test report outline with executive summary, technical findings, risk ratings, evidence, and remediation sections.

prompt_templates.title: Review Scope and Safety
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this assessment plan for scope, authorization, evidence handling, data protection, and risky steps that should be removed or constrained.

output_examples.input: Explain the main phases of an authorized penetration test.
output_examples.output: A structured overview covering reconnaissance, scanning, vulnerability analysis, controlled validation, reporting, and remediation planning.

output_examples.input: Create a report outline for an internal security assessment.
output: Executive summary with business impact and overall risk.
Technical findings with affected systems, evidence, severity, and reproduction notes.
Remediation plan with owners, priorities, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Review my proposed lab workflow for safety issues.
output_examples.output: A safety review that flags unclear authorization, out of scope targets, persistence steps, destructive commands, and sensitive data handling gaps.

best_practices: Use only systems with written authorization and a defined scope.
Prefer isolated lab targets when learning offensive security concepts.
Document evidence, impact, and remediation clearly for every finding.
anti_patterns: Testing internet targets without written permission.
Running persistence, brute force, or destructive commands outside a lab.
Treating tool output as proof without manual validation and business context.

faq.question: Is this skill safe for public targets?
faq.answer: No. It should only be used with written authorization and a clearly defined scope.

faq.question: Does it execute tools automatically?
faq.answer: No. It is a methodology document, but it includes commands that a user could run manually.

faq.question: Can beginners use it?
faq.answer: Beginners can study the lifecycle and reporting sections, but offensive commands need supervised lab conditions.

faq.question: Does it include reporting guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It outlines executive summaries, technical findings, risk ratings, remediation, and appendices.

faq.question: What tools does it mention?
faq.answer: It mentions tools including Nmap, Nikto, Gobuster, Metasploit, Hydra, SQLMap, John, and Kali Linux utilities.

faq.question: What should authors improve before publication?
faq.answer: Authors should remove persistence, brute force, destructive, and evasion instructions or convert them to safe conceptual guidance.
